items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I got hip to Dexter Gordon, Charlie Parker, Lambert, Hendricks & Ross and Joe Williams and on and on on.

ctx.x: Yeah, early Brubeck. I was probably ten. And I listened to Brubeck and I was taking guitar lessons, and I think I bought — I didn’t buy it, my parents bought it for me because I wanted it — the “Time Out” album. And I had no idea what they were doing time-wise. I couldn’t — it was brand new to me. And then the next album I got ahold of was Thelonious Monk. So he played in four. But that was a whole ‘nother thing too. So that’s © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
kind of where it started and I got hip to Dexter Gordon, Charlie Parker, Lambert, Hendricks & Ross and Joe Williams and on and on and on.

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I saw Joe Williams sing a lot of times. And I wasn’t just listening to him sing, I would watch the way he would get up from the stool.

ctx.x: Well how the heck does a student these days learn that protocol? You had sort of mentioned that in today’s jazz education it seems that there are some people are now teaching who weren’t able to participate in that learning process. So you have mostly book-schooled professors now teaching another generation.
Yeah. Well it’s hard to teach somebody something that you don’t know about. I mean they don’t know about it. They don’t know about maybe getting kicked off the bandstand. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

You know? “Nice try baby, come back another time.” So that’ll either make you quit or go home and work on it. Or you know I went to watch before I ever tried to do this, I was a fan. So I saw Joe Williams sing a lot of times. And I wasn’t just listening to him sing, I would watch the way he would get up from the stool. I mean you do something a little different when you’re on stage, because they realized that yeah you’re listening to me but you’re also looking at me. So you have to present yourself in a certain…
